key_insight: FutureSim evaluates agent adaptability by replaying real-world events in chronological order, forcing agents to forecast and update beliefs beyond their knowledge cutoff while interacting with a grounded simulation of unfolding information.
problem_solved: Provides a realistic, scalable way to measure how well AI agents adapt to new information over time—addressing gaps in static benchmarks that can't test forecasting, continual updating, or decision-making as events arrive.
method: Build grounded simulations that replay real-world events (e.g., news articles, question resolutions) in the original chronological order.
Require agents to forecast future events beyond their knowledge cutoff while interacting with the stream of arriving information.
Evaluate agent performance by comparing forecasts and decisions to the actual unfolding outcomes across time-aware metrics (e.g., calibration, timeliness, revision quality).
impact: Enables more realistic, temporal evaluation of adaptive and forecasting behaviors, helping practitioners develop agents that remain reliable in open-ended, dynamic environments and informing safety/robustness trade-offs.
visual_elements: Timeline replay diagram showing news items appearing over time with agent predictions and eventual ground-truth outcomes
Before/after comparison chart of agent forecast vs. actual event probability (calibration curves or reliability diagrams)
Workflow schematic: data ingestion (real events) → chronological simulator → agent interactions → evaluation metrics
Heatmap or bar chart summarizing adaptation metrics (e.g., accuracy over time, update latency, confidence revision)
paper_title: FutureSim: Replaying World Events to Evaluate Adaptive Agents
paper_authors: Shashwat Goel, Nikhil Chandak, Arvindh Arun, Ameya Prabhu, Steffen Staab
